reference.name: x6y3 ring as a hardware design

components.control-board: A RISC-Q board (AMD ZCU216): the hub, the clock, and the cores and converters placed on it. The first is board 0, the barrier root; several are joined by RISC-Q's PutLane.
components.core: One RV32I control core with up to 16 channels.
components.dac: One DAC output. `index` is its number on the board. Pulse channels that name it are summed.
components.adc: One ADC input. `index` is its number on the board.
components.stage: A passive point a wire passes through: a feedthrough, an attenuator stage, a filter. No delay of its own.
components.qubit: A qubit. Drive and coupler pulses end here.
components.resonator: A readout resonator. The readout tone ends here and the returning signal starts here.

rules.name: document
rules.message: A hardware design is { kind: "riscq-design", version: 1, … }.

rules.name: unique parts
rules.message: Part id q0 is used twice.

rules.name: known part type
rules.formal: ∀ p ∈ D.parts. p.type ∈ {control-board, core, dac, adc, stage, qubit, resonator}
rules.message: Part qubit0 has the unknown type laser. Allowed: control-board, core, dac, adc, stage, qubit, resonator.

rules.name: position
rules.message: Part q0 needs centerMm: [x, y, z].

rules.name: a board
rules.message: A design has at least one control-board.

rules.name: placement on a board
rules.formal: ∀ p ∈ cores ∪ dacs ∪ adcs. p.board defined ⇒ type(p.board) = control-board
rules.message: Part q0 is placed on qubit0, which is not a control-board.

rules.name: number of cores
rules.message: A design has 1 to 1,024 cores.

rules.name: cores per board
rules.break: six more cores on the board
rules.message: Board board carries 15 cores; a ZCU216 holds 14 (RISC-Q pblocks-bd.tcl: cores pinned to the X0 column, rows Y3–Y7, three per row; the 14-core build is the largest that closes timing (RISC-Q vivado-scripts/riscvsoc-bd/README.md (results of record, x6y3 and zcu216-14q))).

rules.name: converter indices
rules.formal: ∀ b, kind ∈ {dac, adc}. the indices on b are distinct and in [0, 16)
rules.message: Every dac of board board has its own index from 0 to 15 (a ZCU216 has 16).

rules.name: unique channels
rules.message: Channel id q0.gate is used twice.

rules.name: channel on a core
rules.message: Channel q0.gate names qubit0, which is not a core.

rules.name: channel kind
rules.message: Channel q0.gate has the unknown kind laser.

rules.name: converter of a channel
rules.formal: ch.kind = pulse ⇒ type(ch.converter) = dac;  ch.kind = demod ⇒ type(ch.converter) = adc
rules.message: Channel q0.gate of kind pulse needs a dac as its converter.

rules.name: same board
rules.break: dac0 moved to a second board
rules.message: Channel q0.gate drives dac0 on another board than its core q0.

rules.name: channels per core
rules.message: Core q0 has 18 channels. A core has 1 to 16.

rules.name: channel names
rules.formal: ∀ c. the names of c's channels are distinct
rules.message: Core q0 has two channels of one name.

rules.name: one demodulator
rules.formal: ∀ c ∈ cores. |{ch | ch.core = c ∧ ch.kind = demod}| = 1
rules.message: Core q0 has 0 demod channels; RISC-Q builds exactly one (decoder + ADC) into every core.

rules.name: DSP budget
rules.break: every core given four more pulse channels
rules.message: Board board needs about 5497 DSP48E2; past 2786 RISC-Q's builds collapse (RISC-Q docs/dsp/DSP48.md: the 14-qubit SoC's 2,786 DSP48E2 sat on the ~65 % knife edge).

rules.name: wire endpoints
rules.break: drive0 ends at a part that does not exist
rules.message: Wire drive0 joins dac0 and nowhere, and one of them is not a part.

rules.name: wire medium
rules.message: Wire drive0 has the unknown medium copper. Allowed: coax, planar, fiber, beam.

rules.name: route
rules.message: Wire drive0 needs routeMm with at least two points [x, y, z].

rules.name: route ends
rules.message: Wire drive0 must start at dac0 and end at qubit0: its route ends are more than 0.5 mm from them.

rules.name: qubit parts
rules.formal: ∀ q ∈ D.qubits. type(q.part) = qubit ∧ type(q.resonator) = resonator
rules.break: qubit 0's resonator named as its qubit
rules.message: Qubit 0 names a qubit part and a resonator part.

rules.name: qubit channels
rules.break: qubit 0's gate channel removed from it
rules.message: Qubit 0 names no gate channel.

rules.name: qubit channel kinds
rules.break: qubit 0 reads out through its demod channel
rules.message: Qubit 0 drives and reads out through pulse channels and acquires through a demod channel.

rules.name: drive path
rules.message: Qubit 0: no wire leads from dac0 to qubit0.

rules.name: readout path
rules.break: the readout return of qubit 0 removed
rules.message: Qubit 0: no wire leads from resonator0 back to adc12.

rules.name: coupling pulses
rules.formal: ∀ c ∈ D.couplings, π ∈ c.pulses. kind(π.channel) = pulse ∧ π.qubit < |D.qubits|
rules.message: A coupling pulse names a pulse channel and a qubit index.

rules.name: decoder
rules.message: The decoder is one of the cores.

rules.name: one carrier
rules.formal: ∀ ch. every pulse calibrated on ch has the same frequency
rules.break: qubit 0's drive frequency changed on a channel its coupling also uses
rules.message: Channel q0.gate is given two carrier frequencies: 5498857082 Hz for qubit 0 drive and 5332714542 Hz for coupling 0-1. A channel has one carrier.

warnings.name: acquisition window
warnings.message: Qubit 0: the acquisition window opens 0 ns after the readout tone starts, but the tone needs 10.146 ns to reach the resonator and return. The first 10.146 ns of the window hold no signal.

addi slti sltiu xori ori andi slli srli srai

map: instructions and data; the firmware's bit table sits at the top (s2)
write: the batch the core waits for
read: stalls the core until the batch counter reaches TIME_CMP
read: the batch counter (core-local copy, behind the converters by the link)
read: the k-th reporting channel's result (a demodulated bit); stalls until it is ready
read: the bits other cores published on this board
read: a word another core put to this one
write: the channel's registers (posted to its timed queue)
the batch at which the next fire takes effect
play the pulse-table slot written here
slot s: phase, amp, env, dur
write: a put to a group of cores
write: publish a word to every core of the board
write: a result for the host

lean.name: push
lean.doc: Add an element.

lean.name: pop
lean.doc: Remove the least element.

lean.name: PipeConfig
lean.doc: Pipeline constants of the SoC's core build, with their RTL source.

lean.name: PipeSlot
lean.doc: An instruction in flight between the PC stage and register write.

lean.name: Learn
lean.doc: A predictor write that takes effect at the end of cycle `cyc`.

lean.name: fieldRd
lean.doc: Positional register fields, as `DecoderPlugin` takes them for every format.

lean.name: writesRd
lean.doc: `Execute.RD_WRITE` of `WriteBackPlugin`: a load, a jump, an ALU op that writes rd, or a multiply. Branches, stores and fences write nothing.

lean.name: predict
lean.doc: `BtbPlugin.read` at the PC stage: the predicted successor and whether it is a taken prediction.

lean.name: hashOf
lean.doc: `GSharePlugin.hashOf`: PC bits [2, 2 + w) xor the history.

lean.name: applyLearns
lean.doc: Apply the predictor writes that take effect at the end of cycle `t`.

lean.name: busy
lean.doc: Whether a fetch id still has its response outstanding at cycle `t`.

lean.name: arrived
lean.doc: The word of a slot is at the join by cycle `t` (stored, or arriving this cycle).

lean.name: Exec
lean.doc: What the execute stage does in a cycle.

lean.name: advance
lean.doc: Advance every stage but execute by one cycle `t`. `fired`: the instruction at execute leaves it this cycle (so stage 7 is free for stage 6). `mem` gives the instruction word at a PC.

lean.name: Instr
lean.doc: Decoded instruction. Immediates are already sign-extended to 32 bits.

lean.name: bits
lean.doc: Bits `[lo, lo + width)` of a word, right aligned.

lean.name: signExtend
lean.doc: Sign-extend the low `width` bits (1 ≤ width ≤ 31).

lean.name: toSigned
lean.doc: Two's-complement value of a word.

lean.name: Cpu
lean.doc: Architectural state of one core. `regs` holds x0…x31. x0 is never written.

lean.name: Cpu.setReg_zero
lean.doc: Writing x0 leaves the register file unchanged.
lean.statement: theorem Cpu.setReg_zero (c : Cpu) (v : UInt32) : c.setReg 0 v = c

lean.name: Access
lean.doc: The bus access an instruction requests after its register-only part has been applied.

lean.name: exec
lean.doc: Execute one decoded instruction up to its bus access. A load leaves `rd` for the bus.

lean.name: Instr.isSelfJump
lean.doc: A jump to its own address changes nothing. Firmware uses it to park.

lean.name: exec_selfJump_pc
lean.doc: A self jump is a fixed point of the program counter.
lean.statement: theorem exec_selfJump_pc (c : Cpu) (rd : Nat) : (exec c (.jal rd 0)).cpu.pc = c.pc

lean.name: Instr.text
lean.doc: Assembly text for the debugger.

lean.name: Model
lean.doc: Latencies in dspClk cycles. Stage counts follow RISC-Q `docs/soc`.

lean.name: Readout
lean.doc: Result of one demodulation window. Windows of a channel consume their entries in order.

lean.name: DioEdge
lean.doc: The sixteen input lines of a digital channel take `levels` at cycle `atBatch`.

lean.name: ResponseEdge
lean.doc: One change of the sixteen input lines, `after` cycles after the pulse that causes it.

lean.name: Binding
lean.doc: What a fired slot does to the apparatus. `delayPs` is the path from the converter or pin to the device. `detail` is carried to the effect frame unchanged.

lean.name: Queue
lean.doc: One timed queue: the pop cycle of its newest entry and the pops still ahead.

lean.name: Queue.push
lean.doc: Push at cycle `push`. A full queue drops the entry, as a posted write does.

lean.name: Wait
lean.doc: A read that stalls the core until its sink or timer is ready.

lean.name: Landing
lean.doc: Where the four parameters of one fire take effect, in cycles.

lean.name: Beat
lean.doc: A system put waiting at the hub for the arbiter.

lean.name: nextSource
lean.doc: Round-robin grant (PutHub.md): the first source with a waiting put, scanning from the source after the one granted last. With no earlier grant the scan starts at source 0.

lean.name: nextSource_waiting
lean.doc: The arbiter grants only a source that has a put waiting.
lean.statement: theorem nextSource_waiting {waiting : Array Bool} {granted : Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : nextSource waiting granted = some i) : waiting.getD i false = true

lean.name: nextSource_isSome
lean.doc: While any source has a put waiting, the arbiter grants one every cycle.
lean.statement: theorem nextSource_isSome {waiting : Array Bool} (granted : Option Nat) {i : Nat} (hi : i < waiting.size) (h : waiting.getD i false = true) : (nextSource waiting granted).isSome

lean.name: Program.timeReg
lean.doc: Value of the 32-bit batch-time register at a cycle.

lean.name: Program.coreTime
lean.doc: The core-local copy lags the converter-edge time by the link.

lean.name: itemBefore
lean.doc: Events by cycle, and in the order they were scheduled within a cycle.

lean.name: readyBefore
lean.doc: Cores by ready cycle, then by index.

lean.name: Program.boards
lean.doc: Boards of the build, and where a core sits on its board (its hub source and inbox unit).

lean.name: Program.laneSource
lean.doc: The source a frame off the lane enters at board `dst`: the lane from the board that sent it. Board 0 receives only frames that other boards originate; every other board receives from board 0.

lean.name: applyItem
lean.doc: Apply one scheduled converter-edge, link or hub event.

lean.name: Loaded
lean.doc: Outcome of a core-local read.

lean.name: loadIo
lean.doc: Read one control-block register. Halting reads stall until their sink is ready.

lean.name: readRam_writeRam_word
lean.doc: A word read returns what a word write stored.
lean.statement: theorem readRam_writeRam_word (mem mem' : Array UInt32) (address value : UInt32) (stored : writeRam mem .sw address value = some mem') : readRam mem' .lw address = some value

lean.name: initial
lean.doc: Reset state. Every core starts at the base of its RAM with zeroed registers.

lean.name: run
lean.doc: Run until every core has stopped and no event is pending, or a budget is spent.

lean.name: Datapath
lean.doc: Pipeline latencies of the default pulse generator (`prescaleAmp`, no saturation, 16-bit data, memory latency 2). `docs/dsp/PulseGenerator.md`, "Latency".

lean.name: regenCycles
lean.doc: Phasors are regenerated serially, one lane per cycle, through one CORDIC.

lean.name: default_leads
lean.doc: The derived leads equal the constants RISC-Q reports for a 16-lane DAC channel.

lean.name: phase_is_slowest_fired_lead
lean.doc: The slowest parameter of a fired pulse is its phase.

lean.name: pushMargin
lean.doc: Cycles from a FIFO push to the earliest pop: FIFO write, head register, registered compare.

lean.name: popInterval
lean.doc: A queue pops at most every other cycle. The fire-once blank costs one cycle.

lean.name: readyCycle
lean.doc: First cycle at which an entry can pop: after its own push margin and after the blank that follows the previous pop of the same queue.

lean.name: popCycle
lean.doc: Cycle at which a queue entry pops. `offset` is the time register's value at cycle 0.

lean.name: landCycle
lean.doc: Cycle at which the popped parameter takes effect at the converter.

lean.name: popCycle_ge_ready
lean.statement: theorem popCycle_ge_ready (offset push startTime lead : Nat) (prev : Option Nat) : readyCycle push prev ≤ popCycle offset push startTime lead prev

lean.name: popCycle_ge_push
lean.doc: An entry never pops sooner than three cycles after its push.
lean.statement: theorem popCycle_ge_push (offset push startTime lead : Nat) (prev : Option Nat) : push + pushMargin ≤ popCycle offset push startTime lead prev

lean.name: popCycle_spacing
lean.doc: Consecutive pops of one queue are at least two cycles apart.
lean.statement: theorem popCycle_spacing (offset push startTime lead q : Nat) : q + popInterval ≤ popCycle offset push startTime lead (some q)

lean.name: land_exact
lean.statement: theorem land_exact (offset push startTime lead : Nat) (prev : Option Nat) (onTime : readyCycle push prev + offset + lead ≤ startTime) (near : startTime ≤ readyCycle push prev + offset + lead + 2147483648) : landCycle offset push startTime lead prev + offset = startTime

lean.name: land_independent_of_arrival
lean.doc: Two writes that both meet the margin produce the same converter cycle, whatever the link latency that separates them. This is why the posted link can be pipelined freely.
lean.statement: theorem land_independent_of_arrival (offset push push' startTime lead : Nat) (prev prev' : Option Nat) (onTime : readyCycle push prev + offset + lead ≤ startTime) (near : startTime ≤ readyCycle push prev + offset + lead + 2147483648) (onTime' : readyCycle push' prev' + offset + lead ≤ startTime)

lean.name: land_late
lean.doc: A write that misses the margin by less than 2³¹ cycles pops as soon as it is ready and lands late by exactly the amount it missed.
lean.statement: theorem land_late (offset push startTime lead : Nat) (prev : Option Nat) (missed : startTime < readyCycle push prev + offset + lead) (near : readyCycle push prev + offset + lead < startTime + 2147483648) : landCycle offset push startTime lead prev = readyCycle push prev + lead

lean.name: Slot
lean.doc: One pulse-table entry. Fields are the 16-bit codes carried in bits 31:16 of a put.

lean.name: Buffer
lean.doc: Register file of one channel at the converter edge.

lean.name: Cmd
lean.doc: One posted register write, decoded by address.

lean.name: log2Up
lean.doc: Smallest `n` with `2ⁿ ≥ x`, as SpinalHDL's `log2Up`.

lean.name: Fired
lean.doc: What a fire hands to the timed queues: the entry and the start time it captured.

lean.name: Buffer.apply
lean.doc: Apply one posted write. Writes take effect in arrival order. A fire captures the start time of its own beat, then advances the register by the fired entry's duration.

lean.name: fire_captures_start
lean.doc: A fire schedules its entry at the buffer's current start time.
lean.statement: theorem fire_captures_start (b : Buffer) (slot : Nat) : ((b.apply (.fire slot)).2.map Fired.startTime) = some b.startTime

lean.name: fire_fire_contiguous
lean.doc: **Back-to-back trains.** A second fire is scheduled exactly one duration after the first, with no time arithmetic in the control program.
lean.statement: theorem fire_fire_contiguous (b : Buffer) (first second : Nat) : (((b.apply (.fire first)).1.apply (.fire second)).2.map Fired.startTime) = some ((b.startTime + (b.table[first]?.getD {}).dur) % 4294967296)

lean.name: explicit_start_wins
lean.doc: **An explicit start time wins.** Writing `startTime` after a fire discards the advance.
lean.statement: theorem explicit_start_wins (b : Buffer) (slot time : Nat) : ((b.apply (.fire slot)).1.apply (.setStart time)).1.startTime = time

lean.name: fire_preserves_table
lean.doc: A fire changes no table entry, so a slot can be fired repeatedly.
lean.statement: theorem fire_preserves_table (b : Buffer) (slot : Nat) : (b.apply (.fire slot)).1.table = b.table

lean.name: decode_layout
lean.statement: theorem decode_layout (slots envBits data i : Nat) (inRange : i < slots) (fits : (slots + 1) * 16 ≤ 0x4100) : decodeCmd slots envBits 0x4100 data = .setStart (data % 4294967296) ∧ decodeCmd slots envBits ((i + 1) * 16) data = .setField i .phase (data / 65536 % 65536) ∧

qsysasm.machineLine: machine { qubits: 16 total, decoders: 1 total, factories: 1 total, classical_data_bandwidth: 500 bits/us, qubit_routing_bandwidth: 5000 qubits/us, ancilla_bandwidth: 1000 qubits/us, max_parallel_gates: 16 total, gate1q_ns: 40 ns, gate2q_ns: 200 ns, measure_ns: 1000 ns, reset_ns: 160 ns, route_latency_ns: 2 ns, decoder_latency_ns: 400 ns, magic_state_latency_ns: 5000 ns, pauli_frame_update_ns: 30 ns }

refusals.error: line 1: a gadget definition: write its operations out where it is used ("gadget surfaceRound[data: dbase + 9](dbase) spans 2478 ns:")
line 1: a contract for a gadget or program: the machine line declares every service ("spec surfaceRound:")
line 1: a gadget call: write the gadget's operations out ("call surfaceRound(0, 0, 0)")
line 1: a loop: write each iteration out ("for 0 <= i < n:")
line 1: a guard block: put the guard on each statement it governs (… when c[1]) ("when c[1]:")
line 1: "data[i]" has a parameter in its index; QSysASM names concrete qubits only
line 1: "c[i]" has a parameter in its index; QSysASM names concrete qubits only
line 1: a guard is written "when …", as the compiler writes it ("X data[0] if c[1]")
line 1: request_magic's outputs come first, as the compiler writes it: "<outputs> request_magic state=… with <workspace>"
line 1: count=3 but 2 qubits are named
